messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: closure test
parts:
Hi Vicki
I expect the problem is that you have just two occasions. I haven't looked at the original paper, but intuitively the method requires more. In any case, the code is bad for the nocc = 2 case because
 k <- 2:(nocc - 1) misbehaves. So I would just move on if I were you (and leave me to add a warning to the code).
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: closure test
parts:
Checking Otis et al. (1978) p 120: their test is based on the distribution of Qi, the time between first and last
capture for the ith animal caught at least twice. In your case (2 occasions) all animals caught twice necessarily have Qi = 1, and there is no information on closure. My intuition is that it's impossible to dream up a closure test for 2 occasions. If you can get an electronic copy of Otis et al. (1978) it's worth searching for 'closure' - you will find many reservations about closure tests (their limited power and potential for responding to effects other than closure), that should be heeded, and the general note that their methods require >2 occasions.
Murray
